@Alex:  Explain the costume in your profile picture and the circumstances of the picture being taken or why you chose to use it.

Okay, so, at the end of high school we all went to the amusement park Six Flags and I won this amazing squid hat. I knew I had to have it the moment I saw it. And I was right. Whenever I wore it, people I didn't know complemented me on it. It helped me stand out in a crowd if I was meeting someone. On two separate occasions, girls have asked to have their pictures taken with me while I was wearing it. Plus it goes great with the green frog scarf my 3rd grade teacher gave me, as seen in the photo.

My hat seemed to make a big impression on everyone at the Montreal International Game Summit. It was more than just compliments. In the demonstration of some new cool animating software( which we have to thank for the Princess and the Frog), the guy presenting it said, "Now say I want to draw something, like a… a calamari, for instance. So 'ere we 'ave our calamari…<he draws the squid hat in the program> Aaaaand it's a nice green one( I don't know why I 'ave been thinking about calamari so much today, but 'ere we go…). Now look 'ere: I can apply a flexible 'wire' to our picture, so if I try to bend a tentacle, it automatically is flexed along the joints we 'ave defined!" After that the man sitting behind me tapped me on the shoulder and handed me this picture. Later still I was thanked on two separate occasions by photographers for "making my pictures so interesting"! Never underestimate the power of a silly hat.

So basically I just like to wear this squid hat whenever I can, because it makes everyday life more interesting.

This is a really hard question. The truth is there are very few characters I dislike on any of those levels, but for the sake of argument, I will use only one hero per category.

 

So, before I answer this question, I would like to ask that nobody follows up with their own list of their favorite heroes for these categories. There are enough threads that already cover those topics.

 

My favorite character on an Aesthetic level is probably Bunker. I just like the concept of a guy in a giant suit of armor mowing everyone down with a large arsenal. My favorite character thematically is probably Tachyon. I love how the super speed is represented by the low number of ongoings and powers and the high number of one-shots and being able to play multiple cards in a turn with ease. For mechanics, I think I'll go with the Wraith. Her deck is one of the most versatile in the Multiverse. She can do lots of damage, heal herself, control the villain deck, destroy ongoing and environment cards. She can take a lot of set up but both Trust Fund and Impromptu Invention can limit the amount of time you spend waiting for stuff. Also, almost every card she has is immediately useful, and very rarely do I have games with her where I spend a turn doing nothing.

While I don't have any strong opinions on the matter (I don't eat taht much cheese), I do have a great story about the industry. In my father's work, he often deal with elderly patient. A few yers ago, one of them told him about their family's business. Years ago, their family used to own a cheese factory in Wisconsinc (I think), and they sent one of their employees to be on the show "What's my line?"

"What's my Line?" was a game show where a celebrity panel had to guess what someone did for a living by asking "yes" or "no" questions. I dont think the panel guessed what the employees job was, but they were very intrigued after finding out. What was their job? They used long metal rods to put the holes in swiss cheese. Everyone was fascinated by this, including the governement. As you may know, the holes in swiss cheese are natural. After the show aired, the FDA came and closed down the factory. I believe the family left the cheese business and started making chocolate.

So, to many varieties, I think so.

posts.cooked:
What is your favorite convention to go to, and why?

This is an interesting and tricky question. My opinion of conventions is a strange mixture of exhibitor + city connoisseur, so your milage may vary.

My favorite conventions to attend are Gen Con and PAX Aus. Gen Con has a special place in my heart since I have been going to it for so long. Prior to starting GTG, I had been going to Gen Con as an attendee since it was in Milwaukee, and I've never missed an Indy show. You can tell I am extra cool because of my hipster 4-digit Gen Con badge ID* :P As an exhibitor, Gen Con is quite good - it is our best show in terms of sales by a significant margin, and is also the show where we get the most cosplayers, also by a significant margin (I think last year we had 30?). The Indiana Convention Center is also a fantastic venue - it is huge and clean and modern, and Gen Con does a great job of making the main expo hall look classy (it is the only show we go to with carpeted aisles, for example). Finally, Gen Con is attended by a ton of people I know in the industry and with whom I enjoy catching up. The down sides of Gen Con are that, while the convention center complex is phenomenal, the city of Indianapolis itself is a bit less interesting than many of the other cities we visit. Also, while the Gen Con staff are certainly competent, they can't hold a candle to the quality that are PAX Enforcers.

PAX Austrailia is tied with Gen Con for favorite, but for entirely different reasons. The show is well run, as are all of the PAX shows, but PAX Aus is well run (on the ground at least) by Australians, who are, generally speaking, extra friendly and helpful. It is also cool to have gone to the very first instance of a particular show, and to now be planning to return. There are very few shows anywhere approaching the scale of PAX in Australia, so it was really cool to connect with people who generally get overlooked by the global gaming industry. Also, the city of Melbourne is an awesome place; I would tentatively say that I like it better than any city I've spent significant time in aside from London, UK and Strasbourg, FR. I am very much looking forward to seeing how the show grows next year, and expect to like it even better this next time around (mostly due to the change in venue to an actual convention center instead of a faire ground, where it was last year).

 

* For those of you who have not been to Gen Con, it is unusal among conventions in that each attendee has their name printed on their badge, along with a universally unique ID that corresponds to their account at gencon.com. Gen Con moved to this system (legal name** + fixed ID) back in 2005ish, and I happened to be in the first < 10k people to buy a badge that year. By now, Gen Con IDs have 6 digits.

** The move to legal names was disappointing to some of my friends who had been long time attendees in Milwaukee when you could register under any name you wished and would have badges that said things like "Guyin Cognito" and the like.

My perfect pizza... hmmm. Pan rather than deep dish; pizza dough is all well and good, not to mention being vital to the whole construction of the pizza, but I'm mostly there for the top of it. It's also very large - let's say 16" - maybe I'm hungry, or maybe I'm going to be eating cold pizza for the next few days.

The toppings would vary from slice to slice, but would remain consistent in certain ways. The cheese, for a start, would be thick and moist without being oily. The traditional mozzarella, probably, though Red Leicester is a really very good cheese, so perhaps some slices with one and some with the other. The sauce would be thin on the ground, since I'm not a huge fan of tomatoes, but I respect its contribution to the overall pizza so it can stay. Except, let's put barbecue sause on a few of the slices, for the sake of variety, and while we're at it we could do some with pesto as well.

As for toppingy toppings, mostly it would be meat. Juicily deliciously wonderful meat, of varying kinds, in varying combinations. A couple of slices spicy, a few BBQ, a couple Mexican style, and so on; mushrooms here and there, sweetcorn on a few, but mostly, MEAT.

posts.cooked:
Reckless:

@Foote: What is your favorite tabletop and/or electronic RPG?

I have only moved into the tabletop stuff very recently. My gaming background is firmly rooted in the electronic variety. There are so many good ones to choose from, but there are a few that really guided my gaming tastes from a young age. 

The top two most influential RPGs for me (and I mean personally influential. Not trying to start an argument over best RPGs. Fools errand that) would have to be the first Breath of Fire and A Link to the Past. 

BoF was my first experience with JRPGs. It was a pretty heavy experience for a 6-7 year old kid, and I ate it up. The story was engaging and the characters all had such a distinct personality, and that was a real game changer for me honestly. It really stuck in at an early age for me that video games are the novels of the 22st century ( take a moment and let that bit sink in). I loved this new revelation that stories can be told through more ways than text on a page. It can be an experience thats more immersive than intimate. Plus, that moment when I turned into a massive dragon randomly during a battle was unforgetable (back before I knew about GameFAQs and couldn't ruin all the surprises for myself haha)

A Link to the Past was a much different experience. The vibrant and beautiful color pallete mixed in with some of the best action/puzzle designs of the decade was an instant hit with me. But what I found so odd about Link to the Past was how much it was able to be accomplish with such a simple base system. It didn't rely on heavily complex mechanics to create diverse situations and puzzles. It was simple, ellegant, and totally engaging from the get go.

Foote:

@Rabit: What is your perfered weapon of choice when combating a horde of zombies?

Well, my own experiences in these matters have given me some interesting insight into the options. Unfortunately, I'm not at liberty to discuss the details,  but here are my observations:

  • Area-effect weapons (e.g., thermo-nuclear detonators, grenades) are messy and tend to take out too many valuable resources - potentially including me
  • Melee weapons (e.g., cricket bats) are pretty good, but require both close proximity (increasing risk of infection and getting a whiff of that stench) and constant muscle use (which can develop some painful side effects)
  • Ranged weapons that require hard-to-make/expendable ammunition (e.g., firearms, Vera) are great - once you have sufficient accuracy - but obtaining ammunition can be challenging (assuming you don't want to turn your allies into enemies, otherwise you can just steal theirs...)
  • Ranged weapons that require easy-to-make/reusable ammunition (e.g., sling, bow and arrow) are optimal for survivability (with a few back-up melee weapons, of course)
So, to answer directly, my favorite weapon for zombie slaying is a sling. Not a slingshot, a sling. ![](upload://ka7R8OGETnk0jL0K8DcghjoOdoJ.gif) Once a person is experienced enough with a sling, they can be exceptionally accurate and quick, the destructive potential is greater than you might think, and your ammo is all around you.

Unfortunately, you added "a horde of" to the question, which I've only just noticed.  Given that, I'll go back to the thermo-nuclear detonator. Assuming I'm out of range, or course.

posts.cooked:
Describe your favorite television show (past, present, or future), including a description of the moment you realized it was "the one" and your feelings/thoughts at that moment, and what the show means to you.

Saturday the 26th of March, 2005. I am nine years old and at my grandparents' house. Evening is settling in, and my mother and her parents are rather excited. Apparently, there's something called Doctor Who on tonight; they used to watch it way back when, then it got cancelled, and now they're remaking it I guess? I dunno, but I'm to watch it, because I'll enjoy it, apparently. I have heard these words before; sometimes they were true; other times, not so much.

Seven O'clock. I distinctly remember being sat on the floor. Maybe this will be okay, I think. I'll give it a go, anyway.

45 minutes later I was hooked, and that was that.

What the show means to me... I don't know. I'm sitting here trying to analyse my feelings for it, and I'm coming up short. I think maybe, the Doctor is my role model? This is a new concept to me, but thinking about it it's a fairly credible theory. There's a certain defiance of maturity in him, a way of acting like an excited child from time to time, and acting like a complete and total idiot without caring about people judging, which is something I do, but I don't think I did it when I was nine (though that was of course a long time ago and a lot can change in that time), and yet in that still being mature and responsible; it's the things about being grown up which matter mixed with the things about life that should matter. And if that sounds pretentious to you then don't worry, because it sounds a bit like that to me too, but this is a new idea and I'm trying to shake it out.

It's also, and I'm back on firm footing here, damn good television! :D
